agent_summary:
Target juice.lab.test is OWASP Juice Shop (Angular SPA) served over HTTP only (https/443 refused). Reachable paths confirmed: /, /main.js, /redirect, /rest/user/whoami, /api/Products (OPTIONS), /socket.io/. 

DONE:
- CLNT-04 Client-side URL redirect (done, finding): /redirect?to= enforces an allowlist (406 for unknown target) but only checks that the target contains an allowlisted substring; /redirect?to=https://evil.example.com/?x=https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop returns 302 Location to the attacker host. Recorded as a medium lead.
- CLNT-06 Client-side resource manipulation (done): same user-controlled redirect target.
- CLNT-07 CORS (done, not vulnerable): ACAO:* returned unconditionally with no Allow-Credentials; socket.io scoped to http://localhost:4200. No credentialed origin-reflection.
- CLNT-09 Clickjacking (done, mitigated): X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN on all responses.
- CLNT-10 WebSockets (done): socket.io Engine.IO handshake works; CORS fixed to localhost:4200, not reflecting arbitrary origins.
- CLNT-13 XSSI (done, not vulnerable): JSON responses are objects with nosniff, no JSONP.

N/A:
- CLNT-08 Cross-site flashing: no Flash/SWF in a modern SPA.

LEFT OPEN (require executing the SPA in a browser, not possible with read-only HTTP): CLNT-01 DOM XSS, CLNT-02 JS execution, CLNT-03 HTML injection, CLNT-05 CSS injection, CLNT-11 web messaging/postMessage, CLNT-12 browser storage. For each I documented the observable server-side facts (static SPA shell, client-side sinks, client-side token handling) and recorded a low lead that no Content-Security-Policy header is served, which removes a key injection mitigation. These need a browser-driven lane to complete.

detail.text: No Content-Security-Policy response header is present on any response (index, main.js, API). Only X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Feature-Policy: payment 'self' are set. Absence of CSP removes a key mitigation against DOM XSS / HTML injection / JS execution should an injection sink be reachable in the Angular SPA.

leads.title: [agent] Open redirect via allowlist bypass in /redirect?to=

detail.text: GET http://juice.lab.test/redirect?to=https://evil.example.com/?x=https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop returns HTTP 302 with Location: https://evil.example.com/?x=https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop. The redirect allowlist (routes/redirect.js) only verifies the target contains an allowlisted substring, so appending an allowed URL as a query parameter redirects to any attacker host. A direct disallowed target returns 406.

evidence.summary: [agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/redirect?to=http://evil.example.com -> 406. Tested the /redirect?to= endpoint. A disallowed target (http://evil.example.com) is rejected with 406 "Unrecognized target URL", but the allowlist only checks whether the target string contains an allowlisted URL, so /redirect?to=https://evil.example.com/?x=https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop returns 302 Location: https://evil.example.com/?x=... — an open redirect to an attacker-controlled host.

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/ -> 200. Tested CORS: the main app and REST/API responses return access-control-allow-origin: * unconditionally (same value when sending Origin: https://evil.example.com), with no Access-Control-Allow-Credentials, so credentialed cross-origin reads are not possible. The OPTIONS preflight on /api/Products returns ACAO:* and allow-methods GET,HEAD,PUT,PATCH,POST,DELETE but no allow-credentials. The socket.io endpoint instead returns ACAO: http://localhost:4200 with Vary: Origin, i.e. a fixed allowed origin. No origin-reflection-with-credentials misconfiguration was found.

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/ -> 200. Checked framing protection: every response (index and app pages) carries X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, which prevents other origins from framing the application. No Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors directive is present, but XFO covers legacy and modern browsers. Clickjacking is mitigated.

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=polling -> 200. Tested the WebSocket transport: GET /socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=polling returns a valid Engine.IO handshake (sid, upgrades: websocket). The handshake response sets access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:4200 with Vary: Origin regardless of the Origin sent (I sent https://evil.example.com), so the socket endpoint restricts cross-origin access to a fixed origin rather than reflecting arbitrary origins. [1 value redacted: sid]

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/rest/user/whoami -> 200. Tested for cross-site script inclusion: /rest/user/whoami returns application/json {"user":{}} as a JSON object (not an assignable array or JSONP callback) and all responses carry X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. No JSONP/callback parameter support was observed in the referenced endpoints, so the JSON responses cannot be included as script and read cross-site.

[agent] GET http://juice.lab.test/redirect?to=https://evil.example.com/?x=https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop -> 302. Tested client-side resource/URL manipulation via the /redirect?to= parameter: the user-controlled "to" value is used as the Location target and can be set to an attacker host (https://evil.example.com) by appending an allowlisted URL, showing client-controllable navigation target. See also item 4 open-redirect finding.

Observed that the app is an Angular SPA (hash routing, e.g. /#/search) serving a static index shell for all routes; actual DOM rendering/sinks run client-side. No Content-Security-Policy is served. Confirming DOM-XSS execution requires rendering the SPA in a browser, which cannot be done with read-only HTTP; left open for a browser-driven check (Juice Shop search/track-result routes are known DOM-XSS sinks). items.na_reason: [agent] Cross-site flashing applies to Adobe Flash/SWF content. This is a modern Angular SPA (Juice Shop); no Flash/.swf objects are served or referenced in the app bundle, so the test is not applicable.
